pr_title: Remove slash delimiter from NavigationMesh properties
pr_body:
Remove slash delimiter from NavigationMesh properties.

Fixes #61781

Do not create a pull request for stable branches unless the change is already

pr_comments: See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/61781#issuecomment-1150345153, provided that this works, I think it would be worth doing to preserve some more compatibility for the custom values defined by users (even if they need to be tweaked further). Otherwise as it stands they would outright lose the values when opening the scenes in 3.5 if cherry-picked.

I did some limited testing renaming the values to their old path in the .tscn file. When loading the resource the properties were converted correctly without breaking the resource, including the 2 more special renames

issue_context.title: [3.5 RC3 - Mono] NavigationMesh resource has unusual property names.
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.5 RC3 mono

### System information

Windows 10, Nvidia gtx 1660Ti, latest drivers, GLES3

### Issue description

Firstly, I'm not sure if this is a bug in some parser, intended or ... so I apologize if this is how it's meant to be.

If you check NavigationMesh you will find property names such (__ is a double underscore):
```
public NavigationMesh.SourceGeometryMode Geometry__sourceGeometryMode
public string Geometry__sourceGroupName
public float Cell__size
```

These come from some gdscript names which contain a slash (/) so I'm not sure what is an exact C# format for this that's why I'm not sure if this is a bug or not, I just can't find what else in godot to compare this to.

### Steps to reproduce

Check the NavigationMesh properties.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments:
That is not a navigation issue but I guess C-Sharp API ugliness.

The NavigationMesh exposes scripting properties with a slash which I personally do not like but that is how Godot currently rolles with this. I guess the use of slashes has historic reasons for inspector grouping. I would prefer a general use of underscores for properties that are just a single variable and not a path.
Just to clarify, from what I see at least some of these (with slashes/double underscore) are needed in the script if you use the servers directly.

It looks like these properties were already named with a slash in 3.4, so I guess it's not a regression from the new navigation server?

So we have two possibilities, either leave it be for 3.x and just improve the naming in 4.0 (if not done already), or change the naming now for 3.5 and add compatibility code in `_set` / `_get` to reuse values from 3.4. But the 3.5 release is imminent so there isn't much time to do this.

I'd personally see it the naming changed with 3.5 since it already brings changes to the navigaiton which people will have to deal with anyway (sure it's back-compatible with previous way but navigation server is new in itself), 4.0 is still far away and the new server was a backport from 4.0 so it might be confusing changing one and not the other but well I'm just reporting it so if it's extra work not worth it it's always up to you guys and girls who actually do the work here ;-).

Not sure about <3.5 compatibility and adding so many setter and getters as we already broke the resource compatibility in 3.5 by changing the default properties and the clamp errors a little in multiple PRs and the NavigationServer needs a proper cell size set for merging so all old NavigationMesh resources need to be updated and rebaked by users anyway. The dedicated set and get functions are still the same for the properties so some compatibility remains.

I'm not sure if I I should report this to reopen this or open a new issues so I'd like to ask, I noticed more unusual names in the RC4, in this case it's on KinematicBody, for example Collision__safeMargin, Motion__syncToPhysics. Again double underscores. I'm not really sure how to check the api for more appereances, I use a decompiler in my IDE to check it out but I right now don't know how to search the whole appi at least for these double underscore cases to report them all.

Should I open a new issue, please? @akien-mga
@viksl I think those cases are already reported in #17558 so there's no need to open a new issue, but thank you for taking a look.
Oh thanks, I'm and idiot. Sorry for polluting it here. Have a nice day :)
